A1.justification: Both readable 17-page PDFs describe Drift-AR and support reliable comparison. Pages 2–17 have identical text and rendered content. Neither PDF contains appendices; the supplementary material mentioned in Section 5.3 is absent from both supplied files.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, five component ablations, decoder-step and variance-sensitivity analyses, and entropy–prediction-error analysis in Section 5, Tables 1–4, and Figure 2.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original experimental results and analyses in Section 5, Tables 1–4, and Figure 2.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains identical entropy-informed speculative decoding, entropy-parameterized drifting decoder, training losses, two-phase schedule, and inference stopping procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ImageNet 256×256 class-conditional generation, GenEval and MJHQ-30K text-to-image evaluation, and the same entropy diagnostics. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical: Table 1 retains DMD and LazyMAR for MAR, and SD and DMD for TransDiff; Table 2 retains SD and DMD for NextStep-1. Original-model baselines and Table 3 decoder comparisons also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 5.1–5.4 retain the same model configurations, training settings, metrics, ImageNet evaluation count of 50,000 images, and ablation and decoder-step protocols.

E4.justification: The five component ablations, decoder-step comparison, maximum-variance sensitivity study, and entropy–prediction-error analysis are identical in both versions.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including the error bars displayed in Figure 2. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–4 and qualitative findings in Figures 1, 2, and 4 are unchanged. For example, TransDiff-H with Drift-AR retains FID 1.57, IS 298.1, and 5.06× speedup.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10, mathematical definitions, and the anti-symmetry and stationary-prior equilibrium arguments are identical. No formal assumption, derivation, or proof changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about entropy unifying both acceleration stages, single-step decoding without distillation, and 3.8–5.5× speedup while matching or surpassing original quality.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and result interpretations are identical. Both retain the same limitations concerning attention-based entropy under distribution shift, training duration, and extension to video or higher resolutions.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain identical, including the six-block TransDiff draft model, AdamW settings, batch size, variance and kernel parameters, and training schedule. Both retain the same promise of future code availability.

R1.justification: The 42 references, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to speculative decoding, diffusion distillation, and drifting models are unchanged.

P1.justification: On page 1, v3 corrects 'Behang University' to 'Beihang University' and adds a dagger identifying Jie Huang as project leader. The version/date stamp changes; body wording and section structure remain identical.

P2.justification: The new project-leader footnote slightly shifts the first-page abstract and introduction. All figures, tables, captions, and page layouts from pages 2–17 are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects an affiliation typo and clarifies project-leader credit, but the scientific text, evidence, figures, reproducibility details, and limitations are unchanged. These limited front-matter edits do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
